newsitem.title: USA: Texas dryland wheat needs rain, insects increase.
newsitem.headline: Texas dryland wheat needs rain, insects increase.

text.p: Dryland wheat in Texas was stressed and needed rain, while irrigated fields made good progress, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said Monday in its weekly crop report.
"Insect problems were beginning to increase in some fields," the report said.

As of Sunday, wheat condition had decreased slightly with 55 percent rated good to excellent, 37 fair, seven poor and one very poor. A week ago, 57 percent was rated good to excellent, 36 fair, six poor and one very poor.

"Across north and south central Texas, fields continued to head. Most fields in these areas were showing good yield potential. However, isolated fields had significant rust problems," the report said.
Four percent of the wheat had headed, unchanged from a year ago and the five-year average.
Corn planting was active in the north and south central areas, but cool soil temperatures slowed emergence in some areas. Corn was rated nine percent excellent, 38 good, 39 fair and 14 poor.
Cotton was five percent planted, versus nine a year ago and the 10 percent average. Scattered wet fields slowed progrss.

Grain sorghum planting increased late in the week in central and southern areas. Early-planted fields were emerging with good stands. Sorghum was rated 14 percent excellent, 67 good, 10 fair and nine poor.
Ranges and pastures were rated 10 percent excellent, 31 good, 39 fair, 14 poor and six very poor.
